title: Electrophysiology Protocol for Cortical Cultures
author: Yasmin Bar El
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tqeemte
materials: Use MC-RACK data acquisition software by Multichannel Systems to record the voltage signals and the triggers applied on the culture. For detailed use of the software, see MC-Rack manual.

steps.title: Prepare MEA and amplifier
steps.instruction: Place the chosen MEA (60MEA200/30iR‑Ti‑gr or 60MEA500/30iR‑Ti‑pr; Multichannel Systems) in the recording chamber and install the low‑noise pre‑amplifier board (MEA‑1060‑BC; gain ×1100; Multichannel Systems).

steps.title: Set up camera for calcium imaging
steps.instruction: Position the amplifier beneath the microscope, connect the camera to the MC‑card in the computer and to the stimulator as described in the MEA manual, and configure the system to record camera timestamps and receive an external trigger for camera start.

steps.title: Connect stimulus generator
steps.instruction: Attach the four‑channel stimulus generator (STG 2004; Multichannel Systems) to the computer, the MEA amplifier, and the camera, following the cable‑connection instructions in the Multichannel Systems manual.

steps.title: Select stimulation electrodes
steps.instruction: Open the ‘MEA select’ tool in the MC‑stimulus software and choose the electrodes that will deliver the electrical stimulation.

steps.title: Program stimulation and trigger
steps.instruction: In MC‑stimulus software: (1) configure an external trigger to activate the camera; (2) program the stimulation protocol – rectangular, biphasic 400 µs current pulses of 25‑35 µA (equivalent to 1.4‑1.7 mC cm⁻²) delivered at 2‑40 Hz.

steps.title: Reference manuals and software
steps.instruction: Consult the Multichannel Systems manuals (available at https://www.multichannelsystems.com/downloads/documentation) for detailed cable connections, software operation, and troubleshooting.
